newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equity funds maintain strong growth.
newsitem.headline: German equity funds maintain strong growth.

text.p: German investors are turning more and more to equity funds, as over 7.7 billion marks flowed into managed funds here in the first nine months of 1996, said the German association of investment managers (BVI) on Tuesday.

In a report the BVI said that the total amount of managed funds, in various guises as equity funds, mixed funds, property funds, and bond-backed funds in Germany, grew 13.4 percent to 421.6 billion marks in the first nine months of 1996.
Although bond-backed funds still lead strongly in terms of the absolute amount invested, it is in the increasingly-fashionable equities ar evident.

German investors are becoming more and more interested in equity funds, especially younger investors, who weigh up risk versus reward and opt for less-predictable equity-based investment options, which often offer higher rates of return.
Traditionally, the German investor has favoured fixed return or low risk products, such as bond-backed investment funds.

The change in investor interest is obvious from the BVI figures. While equity funds started the year off quietly, with inflows of 186.5 million marks, they jumped to 756.7 million marks in the second quarter and stabilised at 724.7 million marks in the third quarter.

There was strong investor interest in international equity funds, said the BVI, particularly Asian funds. A total of over 1.7 billion marks was invested in international equity funds in the first nine months of this year.
Investment funds based on the German domestic market saw net outflows in the first half of the year, which turned into investment of 53.7 million marks in the third quarter of this year.

In terms of total amounts invested, German-focused funds still led the pack in the equity funds area at the end of September 1996 with 34.9 billion marks, between 108 funds, up from 29.7 billion marks a year ago.

These were followed by specialised international equity funds with 20.8 billion marks between 160 funds, up from 15.8 billion a year previously. 58 general funds with international focus came third with 5.2 billion marks under management, up from 3.7 billion.
At the same time, bond-backed funds in the first nine months of 1996 have seen outflows of 932.8 million marks.

Domestic bond-backed funds turned over 2.8 billion marks in the year to the end of September, while bond-based funds with an international focus were had outflows of 3.7 billion marks in the year to the end of September.

The total invested in domestic bond-backed funds was 141.5 billion marks, up from 130.5 billion marks, while the total invested in international bond-based funds was 89 billion marks, up from 86.4 billion marks.

Money market mutual funds, or unit trusts, saw return flow of funds of 7.2 billion marks in the first three quarters of the year, driven mainly by the low interest rate environment since the beginning of the year, the BVI said.
Year-on-year, money market mutual funds saw the amount under management at the end of the first nine months of 1996 increase to 51.8 billion marks from 45 billion marks at the same time last year.

Mixed funds have seen inflows of 1.7 billion marks since the beginning of the year and the total under management in the eight funds in this sector had over 7.8 billion marks under management, up 58 percent on last year.

Open property funds were popular with long-term investors, with 12.4 billion marks in inflows over the year, while the total under management grew to 70.5 billion marks in the first three quarters from 55.7 billion marks the previous year.
